thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 ALERT — stratagem (private VPC) — sudden NLB 5xx spike on tenant pool A; DNS TTLs showing concurrent low TTLs from customer side. Paging oncall.
erica: I'm oncall, joining. Can someone paste probe graphs?
sam: linking perf dashboard — https://redwood.ops/d/stratagem/nlb (spike started ~14:02 UTC)
jordan: seeing target unhealthy counts rising, ALB target-group 60% unhealthy, NLB backend connection resets. No config deploys in last 2 hours per deploy-bot.
maria: Customer (Stratagem Inc) reports API errors and retries. Impact: >20% request error rate for private endpoints, some customers time out.
erica: marking customer-impact: partial outage for tenant A. Prioritize isolation. Can we confirm SG changes or recent firewall rules?
kevin-net: I'm looking — security groups unchanged at 13:58. However I see recent DNS change on customer's side TTL lowered to 30s at 13:58 (whoever requested). That could be amplifying failover churn.
sam: hypothesis: backend autoscaler overwhelmed, KV cache thrash + DNS churn -> target toggles -> NLB health flaps. Suggest quick tenant isolation and route traffic to warm standby TG.
jordan: agreed. Plan: 1) Put tenant A into quarantine TG (no shared hosts), 2) shift DNS weight to standby region, 3) open temporary SG egress to monitoring endpoints.
erica: execute. @kevin-net can you create quarantine target group and move targets?
kevin-net: creating quarantine TG and deregistering problematic targets. AWS CLI command: ```aws elbv2 create-target-group --name tg-stratagem-quarantine --protocol TCP --port 443 --vpc-id vpc-0abcd1234``` then ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <orig-tg> --targets Id=i-0123abcd```
kevin-net: quarantine TG created, moving 4 of 6 hosts. Remaining 2 are stuck 'initial' — investigating health checks.
jordan: while moving, I'll create a weighted DNS change to shift 70% to standby region via Route53 — small TTL 20s to make it quick. Command: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://shift.json``` (will push now).
deploy-bot: No active deploys in progress. Last deploy 2026-03-15T09:21:00Z.
erica: DNS shift applied. Monitor error rate and p95 latency. Sam, Jordan — watch for error drop.
sam: error rate dropping to 8% now, p95 latency improving. One customer still reports occasional 502s (likely cached DNS).
maria: notifying Stratagem CS: "we've quarantined tenant A traffic and are shifting to standby region; working on full remediation. Expect stabilization in 10-20 mins"
erica: next steps: 1) keep quarantine TG for 1 hour, 2) run health-check sweep on the two stuck instances, 3) prepare rollback if standby shows regression. Anyone want to add?
jordan: running health-check logs: failing health endpoint returns 504 intermittently — suspect backend process OOM. I'll open a ticket to redeploy those hosts with increased memory after stabilization.
kevin-net: SG temp rule opened: allow outbound 443 to monitoring IPs 203.0.113.45 for 30m. Rule id sg-allow-mon-1782.
sam: metrics look stable now. Recommend we transition to monitoring mode and update incident status.
erica: updating incident status to "mitigated - customer impact reduced; ongoing remediation". I'll hand off to next oncall for follow-up at 14:30 UTC.
incident-bot: Incident updated by erica — severity P1 -> P2 (mitigated). On-call handoff scheduled to jordan at 14:30 UTC.
maria: I'll schedule post-mortem with Stratagem and include action items: investigate DNS TTL change, autoscaler tuning, and dedicated warm capacity for tenant A.
erica: thanks team. Staying available for 10m then off. Good job. :thumbsup:
